Vicki Conley, CANM Artist-in-Residence (2026) The Artist-in-Residence program at Canyons of the Ancients National Monument (CANM), in partnership with the Southwest Colorado Canyons Alliance , hosts artists in a place of “special value.” Featuring the highest density of cultural sites in the country, the Bureau of Land Management (BLM)’s CANM is the ancestral home of 26 tribes and pueblos and protects an estimated 30,000 sites of human habitation. For two weeks, CANM’s 2026 Artist-in-Residence Vicki Conley worked from dawn until dusk to create four artworks inspired by the monument’s rich landscape and found time to host two public outreach programs. “I’m a workaholic and I had to bring plenty of projects to keep myself busy,” Conley said. “I got up at 5 a.m. to work on art and sewing in the morning. Asian American and Pacific Islander (AAPI) history and heritage include experiences of people with cultural, religious, and linguistic traditions from India, China, Japan, Korea, the Philippines, Vietnam, Hawai’i, Samoa, Tonga, among other nations from Asia and the Pacific Islands. It is impossible to tell the experiences of these various groups with a single history. The breadth of Asian American and Pacific Islander experience is a vital aspect of America's rich and diverse past. Explore and be part of the rich history and heritage of Asian American and Pacific Islanders found throughout the National Park System and in communities across the country preserved through the work of National Park Service programs and partners. pages.text: Austrian and Swiss women held captive for more than a year in Niger freed in Libya Skip to content Site search Home News Sport Business Technology Health Culture Arts Travel Earth Audio Video Live Documentaries Weather Newsletters Watch Live Two European women held captive for more than a year in Niger freed in Libya 22 October 2026 Share Save Add as preferred on Google Basillioh Rukanga and Makuochi Okafor , BBC Africa Christoph Greztmacher Eva Greztmacher, 76, had spent many years in Niger as an aid worker Two women - a Swiss and an Austrian – have been freed after more than a year in captivity in Niger and handed over to authorities in the Libyan city of Benghazi. Austrian national Eva Gretzmacher, 76, and Swiss Claudia Abbt, 69, were kidnapped separately in the northern Nigerien city of Agadez in January and April last year. No details have been given about who was holding them or their demands, although some reports have previously linked the kidnapping to Islamic State militants. The circumstances of their release were not disclosed. The Austrian and Swiss governments have both confirmed the release of their citizens. The Swiss government said Abbt was free and on her way back to Switzerland, while Austria said Gretzmacher had been released after "intensive diplomatic efforts". "We are all very relieved that Eva G. is free again after more than 21 months... El cartel se ha de exhibir en un sitio conspicuo donde los empleados y los solicitantes de empleo lo puedan ver. Se tiene que exhibir un cartel en todo sitio de empleo aunque no haya ningún empleado elegible en él. Se pueden procurar ejemplares del cartel preparado por el Departamento (WH 1420SP) para su información o para colgar en el sitio de empleo. Éstos se pueden imprimir a color con un impresor a color o con una versión blanca y negra. Se recomiendan impresores con 1 MB de memoria por lo menos. Para imprimir un ejemplar, favor de seguir estas instrucciones: Se puede disponer de este archivo sólo en el formato PDF. Para ver y/o imprimir documentos en PDF, ha de tener un programa que lea ese tipo de archivo (e.g., Adobe Acrobat Reader® v5 ) y que esté a su alcance en su sitio de trabajo. Pulse en el enlace para el cartel de la Ley de Ausencia Familiar y Médica y espere hasta que salga en pantalla. Close b-jazz Mapper since: May 07, 2017 Last map edit: November 16, 2026 My Story One of things I like to do when meeting new mappers is ask them how they discovered and started contributing to OSM. Well my story goes back to the very, very early days of OSM. I heard about it through some forums (I don’t even remember which) and took a look at it. To say that the tools were in their infancy would be an understatement. There were no aerial images to make use of, things were mostly done through GPS tracks. Living in the heart of Silicon Valley, there were already some roads mapped out. There were areas right where I lived that were definitely wrong, but the tools just weren’t there for me to invest time, so I walked away for several years. Many years later, I was doing some geocaching in my spare time and there was a big stink when geocaching.com moved from Google maps to OSM. At the time, I didn’t get why they would do that. (A while later it became painfully obvious as I realized that Google was charging through the nose for high traffic users of their services.) I didn’t really pick up OSM at that time either. Add another year or two and I saw that Strava had switched from Google to OSM as well and I really started to be more aware that OSM was becoming more and more mainstream. When I retired in 2017, I wanted to have a project to work on so I started learning OSM and finding more and more ways to contribute. Close b-jazz's Diary Cleaning up Golf Courses in the United States Posted by b-jazz on 3 November 2026 in English . Last updated on 4 November 2026. Written 2025-10-30… Published 2026-11-03 About three years ago, during my day-to-day mapping activities, I came across a golf course that had some obvious errors. I didn’t think much of it at the time. Just a fairway that was drawn right across the top of a green. But the more golf courses I looked at, the more frequently I encountered this error. I soon learned about a golf course simulator video game that was built on OpenStreetMap data and was attracting a large influx of simulator enthusiasts who weren’t seasoned OSM mappers. Along with that came various tools to aid in converting OSM data into these simulators, as well as tutorial videos that made some very bad assumptions about how golf courses should be mapped. These factors set the stage for some very bad mapping practices to spread around the world. My understanding is that attempts were made to correct these bad habits at the source, but the tutorial author wasn’t interested in revising or removing his video. Combine that with YouTube’s bad decision to hide down votes on videos, and you’re left with de facto training material that is widely disliked but that new golf course mappers have no way of knowing is a poor source of truth. pages.text: Bangladesh: Wage protests force hundreds of garment factories to close Skip to content Site search Home News Sport Business Technology Health Culture Arts Travel Earth Audio Video Live Documentaries Weather Newsletters Watch Live Wage protests force hundreds of Bangladesh garment factories to close 3 November 2026 Share Save Add as preferred on Google Mukimul Ahsan , BBC Bangla and Koh Ewe Garment workers in Bangladesh stage protests to demand higher wages Hundreds of garment factories in Bangladesh have been forced to close after days-long protests by workers demanding higher wages. On Sunday, protests in the capital Dhaka turned violent with protesters blocking roads, vandalising factories and setting vehicles on fire. They also clashed with police, who fired tear gas to disperse them. Police later said that dozens of protesters had been arrested. Workers are demanding a minimum monthly wage of 30,000 taka ($242; £180), more than double the current standard, citing rising costs of living. Bangladesh's textile industry employs around four million workers and manufactures garments for major global brands including H&M, Primark and Uniqlo. There are fears in the industry that the prolonged unrest could disrupt production and affect international buyers, state news agency BSS reported. The garment industry generates nearly $40bn every year for Bangladesh, accounting for around 10% of its GDP. Secretary of the Treasury Alexander Hamilton stepped forward with a plan to establish a national bank—which still stands in Independence National Historical Park—that would give the federal government more authority to handle the fiscal situation. His proposal incited a debate that tested the US Constitution’s boundaries and laid the foundation for the country’s financial system. NPS Comprised of 2.7 million acres on the Seward Peninsula in northwest Alaska, Bering Land Bridge is one of the nation's most remote national park units. Established by the Alaska National Interest Lands Conservation Act (ANILCA) on December 2, 1980, the preserve aims to protect a landscape that contains an invaluable record of flora and fauna, the history of human migration between Asia and North America and supports an ongoing tradition of subsistence culture. An opportunity to travel to a land visited by so few can provide solitude and beauty not often available in others parts of the country. Proper planning and equipment is needed for a successful trip as its remote nature makes it difficult to call for help and can take several hours to reach medical facilities. Basic Information about Cleanups EPA conducts and supervises investigation and cleanup actions at sites where oil or hazardous chemicals have been or may be released into the environment. Cleanup activities take place at active and abandoned waste sites, federal facilities and properties, and where any storage tanks have leaked. EPA, other federal agencies, states or municipalities, or the company or party responsible for the contamination may perform cleanups. Cleanup can also include site reuse and redevelopment. pages.text: BBC launches educational show in Hausa for millions out of school in West Africa Skip to content Site search Home News Sport Business Technology Health Culture Arts Travel Earth Audio Video Live Documentaries Weather Newsletters Watch Live BBC launches programme for children forced from school by bandits and poverty in West Africa 16 hours ago Share Save Add as preferred on Google Madina Maishanu BBC Africa, Goronyo Ifiokabasi Ettang/BBC Hadiza left school at 13 to get married and now spends her time doing housework As she pounds millet, 15-year-old Hadiza sings the English alphabet. It is a reminder of something that she desperately misses - going to school. "Sometimes I write on the ground to practise and see if I'm still writing correctly," she says. One night, about two years ago, a group of armed men raided her village. "They scared our cattle away and abducted a girl. We had to run away. We walked barefoot all the way here," she says. Since then she has lived in a displaced persons camp in Goronyo, a few kilometres from her home. For a short while she went to school here, but soon met a young man and, at the age of 13, stopped going to classes and got married. "It's tradition here that once a girl is married, her education ends," she explains. Now she lives with her in-laws and helps look after the home. Although Nigerian law prohibits marriage under the age of 18, it is not always enforced. pages.text: Ben Franklin Wasn’t Serious When He Implied the Wild Turkey Would Be a ‘Respectable’ National Symbol … but He Wasn’t Wrong, Either Skip to main content The head of a male turkey is distinguished by the colorful dewlap and caruncles on its neck. Joanna Lentini The wild turkey is a noble beast: the muscular, bronze-sheened ancestor of the barnyard turkeys we eat today. While the two technically belong to the same species, the barnyard variety is relatively new on the scene. People began domesticating wild turkeys in what is now Mexico more than 2,000 years ago, selectively breeding them over generations to become fat and docile. Wild turkeys, meanwhile, have inhabited North America for a much longer time—hundreds of thousands of years. Hunters still eat them, of course, and appreciate the lean gaminess of the wild flesh. But for most of us, the bird is less about sustenance than about a glimpse of the true national temperament: resourceful and restless, by turns noble and idiotic—as liable to swagger into view as to bolt for the trees. This feathery American character has long invited comparison with another native bird. When the Continental Congress first chose the bald eagle for our fledgling nation’s heraldry, Benjamin Franklin wrote to his daughter in 1784 condemning it as “a bird of bad moral character,” given to stealing food from smaller birds rather than hunting for itself. pages.text: Billions of T. rex likely roamed the Earth, paleontologists report | National Geographic Paleontologists figured out how many T. rex lived on Earth—and they found that about 20,000 would have been alive at any given time during a two- to three-million year timespan. Illustration by STOCKTREK IMAGES, Nat Geo Image Collection SCIENCE NEWS Billions of T. rex likely roamed the Earth, paleontologists report The iconic predator’s estimated abundance means the T. rex fossils we have today are exceedingly rare. By Michael Greshko Published April 19, 2021 • 6 min read If you traveled back in time 67 million years ago to ancient Montana, you’d be entering the realm of a tyrant: the iconic predator Tyrannosaurus rex . Before you venture into that lost world, though, you might want to know: On average, how close is the nearest T. rex to you? That might sound like an impossible thing to know—but after crunching through two decades’ worth of T. rex research, a new study provides estimates of the animal’s population density. In all likelihood, a T. rex would be within 15 miles of you, if not much closer. The new study, published last Thursday in Science , also translates these population densities into estimates for how many T. rex ever lived. On average, researchers estimate that some 20,000 T. rex lived at any one time and that about 127,000 generations of the dinosaurs lived and died. Those averages imply that a total of 2.5 billion T. rex lived in the species’ native North America, possibly as far north as Alaska and as far south as Mexico, over a two- to three-million-year timespan.

They are an essential part of American history and embody the strong and resilient characteristics of the American people - so much so that they were designated as our National Mammal in 2016. Once numbering ~30 million and ranging across the United States and in Canada and Mexico, bison were hunted to near extinction, with only several hundred remaining by the 1870’s. Through ongoing conservation work, bison are recovering from a low of fewer than 1,000 individuals. Today, 19 herds in 12 states roam the American Plains. ELY, Nev. – The Bureau of Land Management began a wild horse gather Nov. 14, in and around the Antelope Complex Herd Management Area in northern Nevada, to protect the health of the herd as late season forage declines and winter approaches. The gather will help reduce the risks wild horses face when the range can no longer support the current population. The Antelope Complex includes the Antelope, Antelope Valley, Goshute, and Spruce-Pequop Herd Management Areas. Horses may appear healthy at the start of the fall, but forage and water resources are limited.
